pages.heading: Building a route
pages.body: Aim / use a bridge or ladder builder: $(k:key.use)$(br)Sneak: $(k:key.sneak)$(br)Recipes: $(k:key.jei.showRecipe)$(br)RopeBridge uses the builder item. Macaw's bridges and stairs use normal block placement. Waystones open through Use.

pages.heading: Pack for a move
pages.body: Keep emergency supplies on your person: food, tools, light, fall protection, temperature supplies and the items needed to restart a camp. Put bulk stores and workstations in portable storage. A tent holds a camp; a backpack keeps

pages.heading: Pack for a move (cont.)
pages.body: supplies within reach; a railway moves bulk along a prepared route; a natural Waystone can shorten an established journey. Each solves a different part of moving.

pages.heading: Setting up a tent
pages.body: Craft a tent style and a Tent Mallet. Place the tent on clear ground, then use the mallet on the frame pieces until construction is complete. Use the finished door to enter. The interior persists when the tent is packed. A Golden

pages.heading: Setting up a tent (cont.)
pages.body: Tent Mallet speeds construction. Start setting up while you have time; it is not an instant substitute for getting out of a tractor beam.

pages.heading: Choose the campsite
pages.body: Your tent takes its outdoor entrance's ambient temperature. A snowy campsite stays cold inside; a hot campsite still needs cooling. Tent interiors count as enclosed for hearths. Read $(l:patchouli:chapters/cold#kncraft_tent_hearth)tent climate care$(/l) before a long stay.

pages.heading: Entering the tent
pages.body: Completed tents support seamless entrances and retain their ownership and contents. If a new entrance stays closed, a connected client may still be loading its dimension. Reconnect a stalled client or use the normal tent door.

pages.heading: Canvas from cotton
pages.body: Surround one wool with eight cotton for tent canvas. This saves crafting steps while retaining the original fiber cost. Plant cotton for a renewable camping supply; find the canvas pattern in JEI.

pages.heading: Packing and upgrades
pages.body: Use the Tent Mallet on the door to pack a completed tent. Set it up elsewhere to reach the same interior. Record its Tent ID and keep the item safe. Larger tents use successive size upgrades; later tiers need crossbeams. Tent

pages.heading: Packing and upgrades +...
pages.body: Shovels add floor layers in order, with higher minimum tent sizes. Read the tooltip for the installed recipe and layer limit before upgrading.

pages.heading: Use the tent door
pages.body: Pack and upgrade through the normal Nomadic Tents door. Packing or moving clears the old entrance links; pitching again updates the outside climate source. Keep your route home marked before moving a shared campsite.

pages.heading: A shared camp
pages.body: Gather everyone outside before packing and moving. A player leaving a packed tent can emerge at the old entry location, so do not assume they follow whoever carries the item. Keep the tent carrier and the emergency-supply

pages.heading: A shared camp (cont.)
pages.body: carrier separate when traveling as a group. Test portal, sleeping and temperature behavior in a safe area. The tent's usefulness does not establish immunity to every server threat.

pages.heading: One camp, two locations
pages.body: Pack through the tent door with a Tent Mallet, then pitch it at the next campsite. Check the packed item's Tent ID to keep the same interior. Your furniture stays with the tent, but its ambient climate follows the new outdoor entrance.

pages.heading: First campsite
pages.body: The first tent stands in open grassland. Its doorway leads to the furnished interior shown next.

pages.heading: Inside the first camp
pages.body: Storage, workstations and a central hearth make a portable camp. Leave a clear path to the door.

pages.heading: A colder campsite
pages.body: At the snowy second campsite, frost covers the screen. Moving a tent also changes its source climate.

pages.heading: Inside, hearth off
pages.body: The furnishings remain, but the cold persists inside. The tent shell alone does not provide a moderate climate.

pages.heading: Inside, hearth on
pages.body: The active hearth warms this camp. Fuel, warm-up time and a clear path for its effect still matter.

pages.heading: Cold camp: hearth off
pages.body: The environment readout at the right shows 22 in this capture; the blue body display and frost show cold stress. These are different readings. Your temperatures depend on the campsite and conditions.

pages.heading: Cold camp: hearth on
pages.body: After the hearth runs, the environment readout shows 61 and the central body display returns to 0 in this example. Give the hearth time to work. These readings are examples, not a guaranteed target temperature.

pages.heading: Backpack basics
pages.body: Open a backpack with its assigned key or use it while held. Sneak-use it on a block to place it, then use it as storage. Pick it back up with the supported empty-hand interaction. Upgrade the existing backpack through its material tiers. Keep a clear

pages.heading: Backpack basics (cont.)
pages.body: route through its inventory: emergency items first, then supplies, then collected loot. Color coding makes multiple bags easier to distinguish.

pages.heading: Choose useful upgrades
pages.body: Pickup and Magnet upgrades collect items; configure filters before using them near other people's drops. A Feeding upgrade can keep ordinary food available automatically. Reserve special meals and cures with filters. A Crafting upgrade

pages.heading: Choose useful upgrades +...
pages.body: gives a portable workspace. Stack upgrades increase suitable storage capacity. Refill and deposit/restock tools reduce repeated sorting at camp. Open each upgrade's settings instead of assuming its defaults fit your loadout.

pages.heading: Save food for deliberate use
pages.body: Automatic backpack feeding reserves Golden Apple Stew and enchanted golden apples by default. You can still eat them yourself. Use /kncraft feeding reserved false to allow automatic use, or true to restore protection. The server controls the reserve list.

pages.heading: Magnets near wildlife
pages.body: Deliberate offerings can briefly stay on the ground for a nearby animal. The grace period ends; magnets then collect normally. Filters still apply. See $(l:patchouli:chapters/animals#kncraft_offerings)wildlife offerings$(/l).

pages.heading: Water at a portable camp
pages.body: Place a backpack with a water-filled tank upgrade. Hold an empty waterskin, then sneak ($(k:key.sneak)) and Use ($(k:key.use)) on the backpack. Filling consumes 250 mB of water. Normal clicking opens the backpack; tank capacity and upgrades still matter.

pages.heading: Food and automatic feeding
pages.body: A feeding upgrade avoids KNCraft warming foods while your body is too hot, and cooling foods while too cold. It still honors its food filters and hunger rules. At three hunger icons or fewer, it permits available food to prevent starvation.

pages.heading: Keep deliberate provisions
pages.body: Automatic feeding does not choose the best climate treatment or eat at full hunger. Carry both ordinary food and chosen hot or cold provisions. The default cutoff is body temperature +20 or -20. Check each thermal food in the Cook Book.

pages.heading: Avoid costly settings
pages.body: Void upgrades delete matching items. Test a filter with cheap material before carrying valuable loot. Inception allows controlled backpack nesting, not unlimited bags inside bags. Tank and processing upgrades can support a traveling camp, but

pages.heading: Avoid costly settings (cont.)
pages.body: they need the correct fluids or fuel. Keep a basic hand-carried fallback so one full, misplaced or inaccessible backpack does not stop the entire group.

pages.heading: Keep a totem within reach
pages.body: Inventory Totem can consume a totem in your normal player inventory. A totem stored inside a backpack or Curios slot is not part of that search. It prevents a qualifying death; it does not preserve every item after a death that still occurs.

pages.heading: Iron Chests
pages.body: Iron Chests increases fixed storage capacity through material tiers. Use the appropriate upgrade on an existing chest to improve it without manually moving every stack. Check JEI for the tier path you intend to follow. A larger chest is still

pages.heading: Iron Chests (cont.)
pages.body: placed storage. Breaking it is not the same as picking up a backpack. Empty it or use a supported Carry On interaction when moving supplies; confirm contents after placement.

pages.heading: Moving a full block
pages.body: With empty hands, hold the Carry On key and use a supported block or small creature to lift it. Use again to place it. Shift is the usual binding, but check your Controls. You move more slowly while carrying, and other actions are limited. Use this for

pages.heading: Moving a full block (cont.)
pages.body: moving a chest across camp or into a tent, then put it down. It is a poor last-second escape method. Server restrictions decide which blocks and creatures can be lifted.

pages.heading: Move the whole structure
pages.body: Carry On leaves tent doors and both hearth halves in place. Pack tents through their normal door and dismantle hearths normally. Placed Sophisticated Backpacks retain their own pickup rules. Ordinary permitted chests still move with Carry On.

pages.heading: Build a train
pages.body: Place a locomotive and carts on rails. Set the Crowbar to connection mode by using it on a normal block, then click the carts in sequence without sneaking. The locomotive must be the head. The connecting chain's red marks indicate the tailward

pages.heading: Build a train (cont.)
pages.body: side. Crowbar disconnect and revert modes let you separate or reverse the connection order. Test with an empty train before loading supplies.

pages.heading: Run the locomotive
pages.body: Steam engines need water and burnable fuel, then time to generate steam. Electric engines refill from powered rails; provide charging track before trying to depart. Diesel engines use compatible fuel such as Bio Diesel. Use the engine

pages.heading: Run the locomotive (cont.)
pages.body: interface or assigned controls to change speed, reverse, stop, sound the whistle and operate the lamp. Steam idle holds the train while the engine continues working; stopping and shutting down are different tasks.

pages.heading: Farms can fuel the railway
pages.body: Two Pam's cooking oil and one glass bottle make one Better Minecarts bio-diesel fuel. The locomotive uses its usual fuel and bottle rules. Grow oil crops, process them in your kitchen, then stock a depot beside the railway.

pages.heading: A prepared passenger
pages.body: Cold Sweat already provides insulated minecarts. Carry climate supplies for the station and the walk beyond the rails. Use freight storage at depots and a backpack for the final part of the trip.

pages.heading: Electric locomotive supply
pages.body: This pack's electric locomotive refills on powered rails. Weather2's wind turbine supplies Forge Energy to compatible equipment, but it is not a direct train charger. Plan the track power before starting a long electric route.

pages.heading: Steam controls
pages.body: The author's interface example shows separate water, steam and fuel

pages.heading: Steam controls
pages.body: information. Check those supplies before loading passengers. Match your control bindings to the installed version.

pages.heading: Leave room to turn
pages.body: The author's examples show extra track around return turns. Test the entire train

pages.heading: Leave room to turn
pages.body: through each bend; a route that passes one cart may still mishandle a linked train.

pages.heading: Railways under pressure
pages.body: A prepared line can move people and supplies efficiently, but its track is fixed and can be damaged. Keep an alternate route at each stopping point. Inspect the next segment before accelerating with a loaded train. Signal Rails and

pages.heading: Railways under pressure +...
pages.body: detector rails support junction control. Build and test switches while the area is calm. A railway is infrastructure to maintain, not a way to improvise a route through an advancing storm.

pages.heading: Natural Waystones only
pages.body: Activate a naturally generated Waystone when you find it. Its travel menu connects the destinations available to you; check the displayed cost and conditions before departure. KNCraft disables all 34 Waystones crafting recipes. Survival

pages.heading: Natural Waystones only +...
pages.body: players also have restricted editing and removal. Do not plan to craft a new stone, carry one to a camp or make craftable scrolls as your fallback.

pages.heading: A repeatable move
pages.body: Before leaving, top up food and temperature supplies, choose the destination and check the map. Retrieve loose containers, gather animals and bring everyone out of the tent. Pack it last. Use the route you have prepared: a natural Waystone, a

pages.heading: A repeatable move (cont.)
pages.body: clear railway or overland travel. At the destination, secure the area, place the tent, restore supplies and check that everyone arrived. Keep an exit available before unpacking nonessential materials.
